traits_applied: legend always shown, in plain language
expand every acronym in-frame on first appearance (10Y spelled out in the accompanying caption)

semantic_spec.question: Did Japan's and the US's 10-year yields move the same way between the article's publication date and the reverification date?
must_communicate: Japan 10Y fell back below 3% over 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-05
US 10Y stayed close to its 2026-09-01 level through 2026-09-05
the divergence between the two series is the point, not either series alone
must_not_include: any value not reverified on 2026-09-05 or sourced from the canonical article's own footnoted figure
a single current-tense number without its retrieval date

adjacent_representation.summary: The draft's lead paragraph states in prose that Japan's yield reverted below 3% while the US yield held near its 2026-09-01 level, citing the same reverified numbers.

redundancy_test.q1_new_perception: The reader can see the shape of the divergence — Japan sloping down, US roughly flat — across five actual days, not just read the two endpoint numbers restated in prose.
redundancy_test.q2_harder_without_it: Without the chart, a reader has to hold four separate numbers (JP 9/1, JP 9/5, US 9/1, US 9/5) in their head to see that one line moved and the other did not; the chart makes that comparison a single glance.

qa.notes:
Honest gap: brand_profile is recorded as 'suengj-com' by convention (editorial/profiles/brand/suengj-com.v1.json's declared id/version) but the brand axis's specific token set (palette, chrome level) was not actually resolved into this job's compiled spec -- the SVG uses currentColor only, which is theme-safe but is a minimal-fit shortcut, not a full brand-axis resolution. Recorded here rather than silently claiming full brand compliance; see 06-feedback for the routing note this produces. Actual asset inspection (attempt 1): with y-axis min/max 2.5-5.0, chart-renderer's fixed toFixed(0) tick formatter produced duplicate '3%'/'4%' gridline labels because the five evenly-spaced tick values rounded to the same integers -- a real renderer defect surfaced by inspecting the rendered SVG, not a hypothetical. Fixed by widening y.min/y.max to 2/6 so all five gridlines round to distinct integers (2/3/4/5/6%); this is a renderer-input choice within this job's own compiled spec, not a change to chart-renderer.mjs itself. Attempt 2 SVG (public/media/images/sue570-pilot/news-jp-us-10y-divergence.svg) was recorded at this point as inspected at 2474 bytes: five distinct gridlines, two dash-differentiated series (no color-only distinction), title/desc carry retrieval date, no horizontal overflow at the 720x360 viewBox. That recorded byte count (2474 B) did not match the file actually shipped (2712 B) -- the inspection note was written against a pre-final draft of the render and never reconciled against what was committed. Routed to the renderer layer per docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §5, not silently retried without recording the defect.

CORRECTION (independent review, 2026-09-05, post-publish): the shipped 2712-byte attempt-2 SVG plotted a fourth x-position (x=696, the '2026-09-05' tick) on both series. For the US 10Y series this point was y=126.72, decoding to approximately 4.77% -- a value that appears nowhere in verification-record.json, in any draft, or in any source; it sits at roughly the midpoint of the drafts' '4.76~4.78%' range and was never itself observed or reverified. This violated this job's own semantic_spec.must_not_include ('any value not reverified on 2026-09-05'). Independent review caught this before the pilot's findings were finalized. Attempt 3 (current, accepted) drops the fourth x-position entirely and plots only the three dated, reverified observations (2026-09-01, 2026-09-03, 2026-09-04), each value matching verification-record.json exactly (JP: 3.00% / 2.96% / 2.90%; US: 4.796% / 4.78% / 4.76%); the x-axis now ends at 9/4 rather than implying a 9/5 observation that was never taken. The corrected SVG is 3243 bytes. This correction is recorded rather than overwriting the attempt-2 history above, per the pilot's rule that a caught error is itself evidence worth keeping.
